title: Interleaved Logical Qubits in Atom Arrays
problem: Neutral atom quantum computers require physical qubit movement to perform two-qubit gates, which introduces an unavoidable latency bottleneck and may eliminate quantum advantage in fault-tolerant computations. Existing surface code architectures in atom arrays are movement-dependent and do not scale efficiently.
motivation: As neutral atom platforms move toward fault-tolerant regimes, qubit movement latency becomes a fundamental speed constraint, making movement-free quantum error correction (QEC) architectures critical for achieving practical quantum speedup.
method: The paper proposes a movement-free QEC architecture based on interleaved surface code groups using dual-species neutral atom arrays. Within a group, transversal CNOTs are executed at high fidelity by leveraging asymmetric interaction strengths: interspecies interactions decay as 1/r^3 (long-range) while intraspecies decay as 1/r^6 (short-range). Between groups, interleaved lattice surgery creates high-capacity routing channels for logical qubit communication. The architecture is validated through numerical circuit simulations and benchmarked via compilation of key quantum algorithms.
key_novelty: A movement-free fault-tolerant quantum architecture for neutral atom arrays that exploits dual-species asymmetric interaction scaling to enable transversal CNOTs within interleaved surface code groups.
contributions: Identification that qubit movement in neutral atom arrays sets an unavoidable speed bottleneck for quantum computation
Movement-free interleaved surface code architecture achieving approximately 3x compute time reduction in high-parallelism regimes
Interleaved lattice surgery for high-capacity inter-group logical qubit routing
Tolerance analysis showing the architecture admits 1x-3x error rate increases while maintaining fault-tolerance benefits

metrics.speedup: ~3x reduction in compute time vs. movement-based architectures in high-parallelism regimes

limitations: The architecture requires experimentally demonstrated dual-species atom arrays with specific error rate targets not yet routinely achieved at scale.
primary_theme: Movement-free fault-tolerant quantum architecture for neutral atom arrays
